newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end sharply higher on technicals.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end sharply higher on technicals.

text.p: Mexican stocks rose sharply on Thursday on selective bargain-hunting prompted by technical factors.

"Share prices had fallen enough to make them attractive in some cases. It was a technical rebound rather than due to fundamentals," said Jaime Fernandez an equity analyst at the Interacciones brokerage in Mexico City.
The leading IPC share index ended up 44.47 points, or 1.18 percent, at 3,806.96. Volume was lackluster with 75.4 million shares changing hands.
Telecomms firm Telmex L shares did the most to bolster the market, gaining 16 centavos (2 cents) to 15.70 pesos ($1.95).
Notable gainers at relatively brisk trade also included financial group GFB, retail group Cifra and holding company Grupo Carso.
"GFB had lagged behind gains notched up by Banacci, so it was mainly technical," Jaime Fenandez said.
Banacci B class shares fell 20 centavos (2 cents) to 18.60 pesos ($2.32).

GFB B shares gained 9 centavos (1 cent) to 3.08 pesos (38 cents), Cifra B shares ended up 40 centavos (5 cents) at 12.50 pesos ($1.56) and Grupo Carso A1 shares climbed 2.30 pesos (29 cents) to 45 pesos ($5.60).
Traders said Cifra gained after the firm posted better-then-expected earnings in early trade.
Traders viewed with extreme concern Thursday's vote by a U.S. House panel to overturn President Clinton's certification of Mexico as drug war ally.
"Stocks gained despite the vote, but the outlook for a full House vote is not good, and that's making dealers nervous," a trader said.
Among declining stocks, corn flour and tortilla maker Maseca B topped the percentage decliners' list and was also the most active stock, accounting for some 13 percent of all shares traded.
Maseca B class shares slumped 44 centavos (5 cents) to 8.16 pesos ($1.02) on several recent recommendations cuts and a possible share buyback announced by the company.
Vitro nominal shares fell 1.05 pesos (13 cents) to 20.15 pesos ($2.51) at heavy trade after the glassmaker posted a heavy loss of 3.8 billon pesos ($473 million) for 1996.
